A mobile bookfair in a truck keeps moving in five neighbouring cities V, X, Y, Z, and A for a few weeks. In the current year, it started in city Z on Friday, 12th March. It did not stay in a city for more than one day consecutively, except for city A, and stayed in each city for a total of 7 days. The organizers numbered the weeks to keep a track of their sales: from 12th March to 18th March, it was week 1, 19th March to 25th March was week 2, 26th March to 1st April was week 3, 2nd April to 8th April was week 4, and so on. On each of these weeks, it took an off on Sundays.

(i) It stopped in city Z on dates that are multiples of 4 but not on a Thursday.

(ii) It stopped in city Y only on dates that are prime numbers.

(iii) On Thursdays, it stopped in city X only.

(iv) In April, it stopped in city X on Saturdays. It did not stop in city X on 17 April.

(v) It stopped in city V on all adjacent dates to the ones it stopped in city X but not on the even dates.

(vi) It did not stop in city V on even dates. It stopped in city V on two Mondays but not in April.

 

In which of the following cities did the truck stay for more than two days in the same week?

• The correct answer is option 'A' that is ' Himachal Pradesh'.
  • The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve (CDBR) in Himachal Pradesh has been designated a World Network of Biosphere Reserves (WNBR) site by UNESCO.

Key Info

  • This inclusion adds to India's total of 13 biosphere reserves recognized by WNBR.
  • CDBR spans 7,770 sq km in the Lahaul-Spiti district, featuring diverse ecosystems such as windswept plateaus, glacial valleys, and high-altitude deserts.
  • The region is zoned into core (2,665 sq km), buffer (3,977 sq km), and transition (1,128 sq km) areas, promoting conservation and community participation.
  • The reserve is home to 655 herbs, 41 shrubs, and 17 tree species, including endemic and medicinal plants.
  • Wildlife includes 17 mammal species (such as snow leopards and Himalayan ibex) and 119 bird species.
  • Approximately 12,000 residents engage in traditional practices like pastoralism, farming, and herbal medicine, influenced by Buddhist traditions.
  • The designation aims to encourage international research collaborations, promote eco-tourism, and enhance climate resilience in the Himalayas.

questions.question: As per the revised liquidity management framework, which rate will continue to serve as the operating target of the RBI’s monetary policy?
questions.explanation:
• The correct answer is option 'C' that is 'Weighted Average Call Rate (WACR)'.
  • The RBI will continue using the overnight Weighted Average Call Rate (WACR) as the operating target of the monetary policy.
  • It reflects the average interest rate at which banks lend and borrow overnight funds from each other.
  • By controlling WACR through liquidity operations, the RBI ensures effective monetary policy transmission in the money market.

Key Info: 

  • The symmetric corridor system will remain in place, with the repo rate at the center, while the standing deposit facility (SDF) and marginal standing facility (MSF) serve as the lower and upper bounds, respectively.
  • The Reserve Bank has discontinued 14-day variable rate repo (VRR) and reverse repo (VRRR) operations for short-term liquidity management.
  • Management of short-term liquidity will shift primarily to 7-day VRR/VRRR and other operations from overnight up to 14 days.
  • Open market operations (OMOs), long-term VRR/reverse repo operations, and forex swap auctions will still be used for managing durable liquidity.
  • The requirement to maintain a minimum of 90% of the prescribed cash reserve ratio (CRR) daily will continue.
  • Standalone Primary Dealers (SPDs) will have access to SDF, overnight reverse repo, and all repo operations regardless of tenor.

questions.question: What is the full form of SORR, which is set to replace MIBOR as India’s key interest rate benchmark?
questions.explanation:
• The correct answer is option 'B' that is 'Secured Overnight Rupee Rate'.
  • The Secured Overnight Rupee Rate (SORR) is India’s upcoming benchmark interest rate, designed to replace MIBOR (Mumbai Interbank Outright Rate).
    Unlike MIBOR, which is based on unsecured interbank transactions, SORR is derived from secured overnight lending backed by government securities, making it more transparent, reliable, and reflective of true market liquidity.

Key Info: 

  • India is transitioning from the MIBOR to the SORR as part of efforts to modernize its financial benchmark system.
  • SORR, being a secured overnight rate, reflects broader market liquidity and includes both bank and non-bank participants, making it more representative and transparent compared to MIBOR.
  • The global financial system is transitioning from LIBOR to more reliable and transaction-based benchmarks.
  • Similarly, India is moving from MIBOR to SORR to ensure consistency with international standards and reduce reliance on a small base of unsecured interbank transactions.
  • MIBOR depends largely on a small volume of unsecured interbank transactions, while SORR reflects a broader market, incorporating non-bank entities.
  • This makes SORR a more comprehensive indicator of actual market liquidity conditions.

questions.question: NABARD was established on the recommendations of which committee?
questions.explanation:
• NABARD was established on the recommendations of B. Sivaraman Committee (by Act 61, 1981 of Parliament) on 12 July 1982 to implement the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development Act 1981.

  • It replaced the Agricultural Credit Department (ACD) and Rural Planning and Credit Cell (RPCC) of the Reserve Bank of India, and the Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation (ARDC).

  • National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD) is an apex regulatory body for the overall regulation of regional rural banks and apex cooperative banks in India.

  • It is under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

questions.question: What is the Ways and Means Advances (WMA) limit set by the RBI for the second half of FY 2025-26?
questions.explanation:
• The correct answer is option 'C' that is '₹50,000 crore'.
  • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in consultation with the Government of India, has set the WMA limit at ₹50,000 crore for the second half of FY 2025-26 (October 2025 to March 2026). WMA is a short-term borrowing facility for the government to manage temporary mismatches in receipts and payments.

Key Info: 

  • The RBI may trigger fresh market loan issuance when the government utilizes 75% of the WMA limit. This ensures that liquidity and financing requirements are met without exceeding short-term borrowing limits.
  • The RBI retains the flexibility to revise the WMA limit after consulting with the government, taking into account prevailing economic and fiscal conditions, ensuring smooth management of government cash flows.
  • The interest rate on WMA is linked to the Repo Rate, while overdrafts attract an interest of 2% above the Repo Rate.
  • This differential discourages prolonged borrowing through overdrafts.
  • Ways and Means Advances (WMA) are a short-term borrowing facility provided by the RBI to help the government manage temporary cash flow mismatches between its receipts and expenditures, ensuring smooth functioning of government finances.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Vishwas Scheme recently launched by the Government of India:

  1. The scheme aims to curb litigation under the Employees’ Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act by rationalizing penal damages.

  2. Under the scheme, a uniform penal rate of 2% per month is applied for all types of delayed remittances.

  3. The Vishwas Scheme is initially active for six months and may be extended further.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: C. 1 and 3 only

The Vishwas Scheme, launched by Labour and Employment Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, aims to reduce prolonged litigations under the EPF & Miscellaneous Provisions Act by rationalizing penal damages for delayed remittances. The scheme simplifies penalties with a graded structure (0.25%–1%), ensuring fair treatment for employers while promoting compliance. It also covers pending, ongoing, and pre-adjudication cases, and compliant entities will see litigation withdrawn or abated. Alongside, the EPFO has liberalized partial withdrawal rules, reducing service requirements to 12 months and allowing withdrawals for education, marriage, housing, illness, and unemployment — improving member convenience and liquidity.

Key Points:

  • Launched by: Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Minister of Labour & Employment

  • Purpose: Reduce EPF litigation by rationalizing penal damages

  • Uniform penal rate: 1% per month (graded: 0.25% up to 2 months, 0.50% up to 4 months)

  • Duration: Initially 6 months, extendable

  • Covers: Pending litigation, unpaid penal damage orders, pre-adjudication defaults

  • Withdrawal reforms: 100% withdrawal allowed for essential needs; 25% corpus retention mandatory

Static GK:

  • Administered by: Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)

  • Act: Employees’ Provident Fund & Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952

  • Launched: During 238th CBT Meeting, New Delhi

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the UDAN Scheme (Ude Desh Ka Aam Nagrik):

  1. The UDAN Scheme was launched on 21st October 2016 under the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

  2. As of 2025, the scheme has operationalized 649 routes and connected 93 airports, including heliports and water aerodromes.

  3. The scheme will conclude in April 2025 with no further expansion plans announced.

Which of the statements is/are correct?

With ₹4,300 crore disbursed as VGF and ₹4,638 crore invested in regional airports, UDAN has become a transformational initiative. The Expanded UDAN Framework (till 2027) focuses on connectivity in Northeast, hilly terrains, and aspirational districts.

Key Points:

  • Launch date: 21 October 2016

  • Total routes: 649 operational

  • Airports connected: 93 (including heliports & water aerodromes)

  • Total passengers: 1.56 crore

  • Viability Gap Funding: ₹4,300 crore

  • Scheme extended till: April 2027

Static GK:

  • Ministry: Civil Aviation

  • Secretary (2025): Samir Kumar Sinha

  • Policy origin: National Civil Aviation Policy, 2016

questions.question: The RBI is planning to revise remittance regulations under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) to curb passive capital export. As per the proposed changes, which of the following will be barred under the new rules, while permissible investments like equities, mutual funds, and property will remain unaffected?
options: Holding foreign equity shares in listed companies under LRS
Investing in foreign mutual funds through SEBI-approved channels
Sending remittances for education and medical treatment abroad
Holding offshore time deposits with lock-in periods under LRS
Buying property abroad under the LRS limit
questions.explanation:
• The correct answer is option 'D' that is 'Holding offshore time deposits with lock-in periods under LRS'.
  • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) plans to tighten regulations on overseas remittances by resident Indians.
  • Proposed changes will prevent residents from holding foreign currency deposits with lock-in periods.
  • The RBI aims to stop overseas transfers from being used as a means to earn interest in foreign accounts, which it views as "passive wealth shifting."
  • India is cautious about rising outward remittances and the full convertibility of the rupee to protect foreign exchange reserves and manage currency volatility.

questions.question: Which of the following wetlands were recently added to the list of Ramsar sites from Bihar?
questions.explanation:
• The correct answer is option 'B' that is 'Gokul Jalashay and Udaipur Jheel''.
  • India’s total count of Ramsar sites has risen to 93 after the inclusion of two new wetlands from Bihar — Gokul Jalashay (Buxar) and Udaipur Jheel (West Champaran).

Key Info: 

  • The two newly recognized Ramsar sites from Bihar are Gokul Jalashay (in Buxar district) and Udaipur Jheel (in West Champaran district).
  • Their inclusion underscores India’s continued efforts in wetland conservation and ecological balance.
  • India now ranks third globally in the number of Ramsar sites (93), after the United Kingdom (176) and Mexico (144).
  • India also leads Asia with the highest number of designated Ramsar wetlands.
  • The total area of India’s 93 Ramsar sites now covers 1,360,718 hectares.
  • These wetlands play a vital role in flood control, groundwater recharge, biodiversity conservation, and climate regulation.

Additional Info:

  • The Ramsar Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran.
  • It is an international treaty focused on the conservation and wise use of wetlands.
  • The convention came into force in 1975, and today over 2,500 sites globally are recognized under it.

questions.question: Which natural landmark in New Zealand was recently granted legal personhood?
questions.explanation:
• The correct answer is option 'C' that is 'Mount Taranaki'.
  • Mount Taranaki, now known as Taranaki Maunga, has been granted legal personhood, recognizing it as a human being under New Zealand law.
  • This status eliminates government ownership, allowing the mountain to possess legal rights and responsibilities similar to those of an individual.
  • Taranaki Maunga is the third natural feature in New Zealand to receive this designation, following Te Urewera National Park and the Whanganui River.
  • The mountain is respected by the Indigenous Māori people as a sacred ancestor and symbolizes their connection to the ecosystem.
  • With its new status, local Māori representatives, iwi, and government will collaborate to care for and protect Taranaki Maunga.

questions.question: Which country does László Krasznahorkai, the 2025 Nobel Prize winner in Literature, belong to?

questions.question: Exercise Bright Star 2025, in which India is participating, is scheduled to be held in:
questions.explanation:

From a bilateral drill in 1980 between Egypt and the U.S., Bright Star has become one of the largest multinational exercises in the Middle East and North Africa. India’s involvement not only demonstrates operational readiness but also strengthens strategic ties with Egypt, the United States, and other partners. Tri-service engagement enhances interoperability across the Army, Navy, and Air Force while providing experience in multinational peacekeeping and coalition operations.

  • Exercise Bright Star started in 1980 as a bilateral drill and is now a major multinational exercise.
  • India is sending over 700 tri-service personnel for Bright Star 2025 in Egypt (August 28 – September 10).

questions.question: The GST Council has approved a new tax structure effective from ______, introducing dual rates of ______ and ______, while also levying a 40% tax on luxury items and specific services.

questions.question: How many members constitute the newly formed Payments Regulatory Board (PRB) by the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation:

  • The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has constituted a six-member Payments Regulatory Board (PRB) to oversee and regulate the functioning of payment systems in India.
  • This board includes three nominees from the Central Government and three representatives from the RBI.

  • The Board is chaired by RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra. Alongside the Governor, the two other RBI representatives on the PRB are the Deputy Governor and the Executive Director in charge of Payment and Settlement Systems.

  • The inclusion of government representatives allows for government input in payment system decisions.

  • The PRB must meet at least twice a year as per a May notification.
  • The principal legal adviser of the RBI is a permanent invitee to PRB meetings.

questions.question: Which of the following best explains what the author is most likely implying about economic modeling related to climate change?
options: Current economic models fail to fully quantify potential GDP losses due to lack of integration of climate tipping points.
There is growing consensus among policymakers that financial risk from nature loss is minimal.
Risk models that ignore cascading and compounding events give an accurate long-term projection of global GDP.
The IMF and World Bank are already adapting models to include ecological disruptions.
Models in use today are primarily concerned with short-term inflation and employment figures.
questions.explanation:
A is Correct:

This option captures the core implication woven throughout the passage: the author, quoting Dr. Abrams and others, consistently criticizes the current economic and climate risk models for being inadequate and dangerously incomplete.

Evidence from the passage:

  • The article states we are “grossly underestimating risk due to climate change and nature-related crises.”

  • It explicitly says models often look only at “rising temperatures and precipitation, and are not factoring in compounding extreme weather events.”

  • There is also discussion of “cascading risks from potential tipping points”, such as the possible shutdown of AMOC.

  • The authors argue for the integration of systemic risks, long-term disruptions, and tipping points into economic modeling.

B contradicts the article’s message.

  • In fact, the opposite is implied: policymakers and institutions are failing to act despite rising risks, not because they agree risks are low, but possibly because models misrepresent the severity.

C is directly refuted by the passage.

  • The article criticizes such models and states clearly that ignoring cascading events leads to underestimation, not accurate projections.

D While this might be true in external contexts, nowhere in the passage is it stated or implied.

  • In fact, the article implies that existing institutions are lagging or relying on outdated modeling.

E This might be true for some macroeconomic tools, but the passage does not say this.

  • The focus is not on what models currently prioritize (like inflation or employment), but on what they fail to include — specifically climate tipping points and systemic risks.

  • So, (E) misses the central issue the article highlights and introduces a distraction.

Hence, option A is the correct choice.

questions.question: Based on the text, which inference can we draw about the urgency of climate action?
options: A transformative, non-linear change is now necessary to protect economic systems.
Incremental policy changes are sufficient to reverse the projected GDP contraction.
Governments must rethink risk like they would for financial system failures.
questions.explanation:
C is correct because Dr. Abrams says climate risk must be treated with the same rigor as financial risk.

The article states:

“Dr. Abrams said there is an urgent need for more realistic risk assessment that accounts for systemic risks and tipping points, with climate risk being treated with the same rigor applied to financial system risks.”

This draws a clear parallel between climate and financial system risk—implying that governments and institutions must adopt a level of seriousness and technical scrutiny similar to that applied in financial regulation.

So, this supports the inference that governments need to rethink and upgrade their climate risk approach to be on par with financial system resilience strategies.

A is correct because he also stresses the need for "non-linear" change to trigger transformative shifts.

The article includes the following direct quote from Dr. Abrams:

“We have left it too late for incremental change. We now need to look at how we can trigger tipping behaviour in order to achieve non-linear change in socio economic and technological systems.”

The use of “tipping behaviour” and “non-linear change” clearly emphasizes that transformative, systemic shifts—not slow, step-by-step actions—are required.

So, we can infer that small or moderate efforts are insufficient. A rapid and large-scale shift is needed to meaningfully protect economic systems.

Hence, option E is the correct choice.

questions.question:
What can be inferred about the risks posed by a potential disruption of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC), based on the information provided in the passage?

a) A shutdown of the AMOC could significantly reduce the amount of land suitable for cultivating essential crops like wheat and maize, thereby posing a serious threat to global food security.
b) The disruption of AMOC is expected to alter regional precipitation patterns, particularly increasing rainfall in North America, which may lead to agricultural surpluses in temperate zones.
c) AMOC disruption has the potential to destabilize key agricultural regions by altering oceanic and atmospheric systems, which could undermine crop yields in already climate-sensitive areas.
questions.explanation:
(a) is correct: The passage explicitly mentions that the shutdown of AMOC “could reduce suitable land for growing wheat and maize by up to half compared to a world without climate change.” This directly supports the inference that such disruption could threaten global food security.

(b) is incorrect: The passage does not discuss rainfall in North America or any specific regional precipitation patterns. This is an extrapolation beyond what is supported by the text and introduces a speculative element not mentioned in the source.

(c) is correct: The idea of AMOC affecting oceanic currents and atmospheric systems is valid. Since the passage warns of decreased agricultural land due to AMOC shutdown, it is reasonable to infer that such a disruption could destabilize agricultural systems, especially those in already fragile regions.

Hence, option D is the correct choice.

questions.question:
From the author’s perspective, what is the most likely outcome if governments continue to delay meaningful climate action?

a) Market-driven mechanisms will gradually adjust to climate-related disruptions, ultimately restoring ecological and economic stability over time without the need for aggressive policy intervention.
b) If decisive policy measures are not taken soon, climate-related economic damage is likely to intensify, potentially reaching a point where recovery becomes extremely difficult or even impossible.
c) Delays in climate response will likely exacerbate ecological degradation to the extent that financial systems will be unable to absorb the resulting shocks, thereby overwhelming traditional risk and regulatory frameworks.
questions.explanation:
(a) is incorrect: The passage clearly criticizes the “market-led approach” to managing climate and nature-related risks, stating it is “not delivering.” This means the author does not believe the market will “naturally course-correct.” Instead, the passage calls for immediate, coordinated, and non-incremental government action.

(b) is correct: The article warns of escalating consequences—such as mass mortality, displacement, economic contraction, and conflict—if the current path continues. These are all indications that the damage will deepen and possibly become irreversible.

(c) is correct: There’s a strong emphasis on how nature-related financial risks are underestimated and could destabilize current economic models. Heather Plumpton even notes that “conventional economic models... don’t take account of irreversible climate tipping points”, suggesting such risks could overwhelm traditional frameworks.

Hence, option E is the correct choice.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank given in the passage with the most appropriate word.

"Dr. Abrams said there is an urgent need for more realistic risk assessment that accounts for systemic risks and tipping points, with climate risk being treated with the same ___ applied to financial system risks."
questions.explanation:
The phrase “treated with the same ___ applied to financial system risks” calls for a noun that conveys depth, discipline, and methodical seriousness—specifically in how risks are analyzed or regulated.

  • “Rigor” refers to strictness, thoroughness, and precision—exactly the traits applied in financial risk management (e.g., banking regulations, stress testing).

  • Therefore, "rigor" fits both semantically and grammatically, and mirrors the tone of scientific and risk-based discourse in the passage.

Hence, option C is the correct choice.

questions.question:
Identify the statements that are true based on the information presented in the passage:

a) The global economy is at risk of shrinking by as much as 50% between 2070 and 2090 if decisive action is not taken to address the escalating threats posed by climate change and ecological degradation.
b) If the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC) were to shut down, it could potentially benefit colder regions by increasing their agricultural productivity and expanding arable land.
c) The failure of governments to adequately respond to environmental degradation and biodiversity loss is increasingly being viewed as a significant economic threat with long-term consequences for national and global prosperity.
questions.explanation:
(a) is True:

  • The passage clearly states:

    “Global GDP could contract by 50% between 2070 and 2090 without urgent action.”

  • This makes (a) factually accurate. The economic contraction is directly tied to climate inaction, reinforcing the urgency of intervention.

(b) is False:

  • The article warns that the AMOC shutdown would reduce suitable land for growing wheat and maize by up to half.

  • It does not suggest that agricultural conditions in colder regions would improve.

Therefore, (b) is incorrect as it misrepresents the impact of AMOC disruption.

(c) is True:

  • Heather Plumpton explicitly states:

    “For too long the government has disregarded the financial risks that nature loss creates, but these are getting too high for our economy to bear.”

  • This clearly shows that government inaction is increasingly being seen as economically dangerous, making (c) valid.

Hence, option D is the correct choice.

questions.question:
The sentence below has a few words highlighted in bold. Check which words need to be swapped to make the sentence contextually and grammatically correct.

“And their frequency (A) and intensity is   disrupt , (B) as well. These extreme weather  homes (C) will outpacing (D) infrastructure, destroy  events (E) and disrupt supply chains.”
questions.explanation:
We need to swap :
B-D:

 "outpacing" fits in the first clause:

“And their frequency and intensity is outpacing as well.”

  • Subject: "frequency and intensity" (plural compound subject)

  • Verb: "is outpacing" (grammatically should be "are outpacing", but authors often use “is” when treating two qualities as a single rising phenomenon).

  • "Outpacing" logically connects with frequency and intensity rising faster than projections.

  • This matches the meaning conveyed earlier in the article:

    “Upfront risks like floods and wildfires are actually happening faster than climate scientists had previously projected.”

  "disrupt" doesn’t fit there:

  • "Disrupt" is a transitive verb, meaning it requires a direct object (e.g., “disrupt supply chains”).

  • “Frequency and intensity is disrupt” is grammatically incorrect and semantically illogical—you can’t say "frequency is disrupt."


C-E:

  • Subject of the sentence: "extreme weather events"

  • The noun "events" is what can logically and grammatically perform the action of disrupting infrastructure.

  • So "events will disrupt" is both syntactically valid and contextually precise.

🔹 Why "homes" doesn't work there:

  • “These extreme weather homes will disrupt infrastructure…” is contextually nonsensical—"homes" cannot cause disruption in this context.

  • “Homes” is the object (i.e., the thing being destroyed), not the subject doing the action.

Hence, option C is the correct choice.

questions.question: Which of the following phrasal verbs/idioms best captures the tone and urgency of the statement : “We have left it too late for incremental change.”?
questions.explanation:
• The context is about facing up to hard but necessary change — that’s exactly what "bite the bullet" conveys.
  • “Turn a blind eye” and “kick the can down the road” imply avoidance, the opposite of the message.
  • “Call it a day” means stop, which is irrelevant here.
  • “Draw the line” is about setting limits, not urgency.

Hence, option A is the correct choice.

questions.question:
Directions: In the question below, a sentence is given with two parts missing. From the options, choose the words that will fit in the sentence to make it correct.

The _______ is on policymakers to ________ that both monetary and fiscal action is focused on reining in inflation.

1. liability, endure

2. gist, guarantee

3. onus, ensure
questions.explanation:
The sentence tells us how the burden of responsibility is on policymakers to make sure that monetary and fiscal action focuses on controlling inflation.

First blank - we need a noun to be modified by the definite article THE. ONUS and LIABILITY mean burden or responsibility and will fit here.

Second blank - we need a base form verb to fit in the TO + VERB infinitive construction. GUARANTEE and ENSURE mean to make sure of something and will fit here. Thus, C is the right answer.

Endure - tolerate. Gist - summary.

questions.question:
Directions: In the question below, a sentence is given with two parts missing. From the options, choose the words that will fit in the sentence to make it correct.

While the bill goes a _________ distance in reining in the relatively ________ sale of firearms across weapons buyer profiles, it falls far short of the critical regulations that must be enforced.

1. considerate, unrestrained

2. considerable, unhindered

3. conventional, unrestricted
questions.explanation:
The sentence tells us how the bill has made significant progress in reining in the relatively uncontrolled sale of firearms, but it fails to enforce critical regulations.

First blank - we need an adjective to modify the noun DISTANCE. CONSIDERABLE means substantial, and will fit here.

Second blank - we need an adjective to modify the noun SALE. UNHINDERED, UNRESTRAINED and UNRESTRICTED all mean uncontrolled, and will fit here. Thus, B is the right answer.

Considerate - kind and sensitive towards the needs and feelings of other people. Conventional - traditional.

questions.question:
Directions: In the question below, a sentence is given with two parts missing. From the options, choose the words that will fit in the sentence to make it correct.

The fact that such a bill passed both houses of Congress and reached the president’s desk _______ the deep shock that the nation ________ in the recent acts of gun violence in a school in Texas.

1. repeals, sustained

2. reflects, experienced

3. reveals, witnessed
questions.explanation:
The sentence tells us how the fact that the bill passed both houses shows the deep shock that the nation underwent in the recent acts of gun violence.

First blank - we need a singular verb to agree with the singular subject FACT. REFLECTS and REVEALS mean to indicate or show and will fit here.

Second blank - we need a verb to agree with the subject NATION. WITNESSED, EXPERIENCED and SUSTAINED all mean underwent and will fit here. Thus, D is the right answer.

Repeals - cancels.

questions.question:
Directions: In the question below, a sentence is given with two parts missing. From the options, choose the words that will fit in the sentence to make it correct.

The law does not hint at ________ the assault weapons ban of 1994, which expired a decade later, since which time this category of weapon has become the most frequently used in ______ mass shootings.

1. Restoring, dangerous

2. Reviving, lethal

3. Revering, deadly
questions.explanation:
The sentence tells us how the law does not hint at bringing back into effect the assault weapons ban of 1994, which expired a decade later, and since then, this weapon has become most frequently used in destructive mass shootings.

First blank - we need a gerund to be modified by the preposition AT. RESTORING and REVIVING mean to bring back into effect or to a former state, and will fit here.

Second blank - we need an adjective to modify the gerund phrase MASS SHOOTINGS. DANGEROUS, LETHAL and DEADLY all mean likely to cause death and suffering, and will fit here. Thus, B is the right answer.

Revering - respecting.

questions.question:
Directions: In the given sentence, two blanks are given, indicating that something is missing. From the given options, choose the combination of pairs of words that can fit in the sentence.

Owing to climate change challenges, it has become _____ to explore _____ and sustainable means of income generation.

  1. imperative, viable
  2. crucial, futile
  3. trivial, yearning
questions.explanation:
The sentence tells us how due to climate change challenges, it has become essential to explore feasible and sustainable means of income generation. First blank - we need an adjective to modify the TO+VERB infinitive construction (to explore). IMPERATIVE and CRUCIAL mean ‘of vital importance’ and will fit here.

Trivial - unimportant, of little value or importance.

Second blank - we need an adjective to modify the noun phrase INCOME GENERATION. VIABLE means capable of working successfully, feasible, and will fit here.

Futile -incapable of producing any useful result; pointless. Yearning - a feeling of intense longing for something.

Thus, (A) is the right answer.

questions.question:
Directions: In the following question, three sentences are given revolving around the same theme or idea. Decide which of the sentences are grammatically and meaningfully correct and mark the answer accordingly.

1. The seasonal rains in March caused a slight loss in output in Punjab and Haryana, but the low temperatures following the rains helped the crops in other unaffected areas.
2. Harvesting of the cereal, which usually commences by April 1, started late this year due to the unseasonal rains in March; farmers decided to let the moisture in the crop dry up in the fields.
3. The wheat stocks had fall to 8.3 MT on April 1, as the government's procurement had plunged to a record low due to a drop in production and increased private buying this year.
questions.explanation:
Option (D) is correct as only the 2nd sentence is grammatically and contextually correct.

In the first sentence, the word “seasonal” is wrong; in this context, it should be “unseasonal” because it implies that the rains occurred during a time when they were not supposed to, and hence caused a slight loss in the output of the crop production in Punjab and Haryana.

The 3rd sentence is grammatically wrong as the verb “fall” should be in the past participle form “fallen”.

The corrected sentences are as follows:

1. The unseasonal rains in March caused a slight loss in output in Punjab and Haryana, but the low temperatures following the rains helped the crops in other unaffected areas.

3. The wheat stocks had fallen to 8.3 MT on April 1, as the government's procurement had plunged to a record low due to a drop in production and increased private buying this year.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, three sentences are given revolving around the same theme or idea. Decide which of the sentence(s) is/are grammatically and meaningfully correct and mark the answer accordingly.


1. The government has announced new rules for the distribution of COVID-19 vaccines, with priority given to healthcare workers and vulnerable populations during the pandemic.
2. After being closed for nearly a year due to the pandemic, the popular tourist attraction will be reopening its doors next week.
3. Profits of the companies making COVID-19 vaccines have seen insignificant increases this quarter after the government announced the distribution rules, which ensured wider reach and created a surge in vaccine demand.
questions.explanation:
Option B is the right answer.

Both 1 and 2 are grammatically and contextually correct. In 3, we need to replace the word INSIGNIFICANT with the word SIGNIFICANT because "insignificant" implies that the distribution rules had a negative impact on the profits of the companies making Covid-19 vaccines, which is not the case. In reality, the distribution rules have increased demand for the vaccines (as mentioned in the sentence) and thus increased the profits of these companies. Therefore, "significant" is a more appropriate word to use in this context.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, three sentences are given revolving around the same theme or idea. Decide which of the sentence(s) is/are grammatically and meaningfully correct and mark the answer accordingly.

 

1. The company is experiencing an acute short of workers due to the current labour market.
2. Many employees have left the company in pursuit of better opportunities, leading to a significant gap in staffing.
3. The organisation is facing a major staff deficit due to the present labour market conditions.
questions.explanation:
Option (D) is the right answer as both sentences 2 and 3 are grammatically and contextually correct.

In the 1st sentence, the word "short" is incorrect in this context as “short” is an adjective that describes something that is not long enough or is smaller in length whereas “shortage” means a lack of something that is needed or required, which goes with the context of the sentence where the company is facing a lack of workers. Hence, sentence 1 is incorrect.

.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, three sentences are given revolving around the same theme or idea. Decide which of the sentence(s) is/are grammatically and meaningfully correct and mark the answer accordingly.

1. The unprecedented levels of carbon emissions released into the atmosphere are a major cause of global warming.

2. The government is being criticised for its lack of action in addressing climate change.

3. The climatic conditions are expected to improve in the coming years due to the alarming increase in greenhouse gases.
questions.explanation:
The correct option is (B), as both sentences 1 and 2 are grammatically and contextually correct.

In the 3rd sentence, the word "improve" is incorrect in this context since the sentence mentions an alarming increase in greenhouse gases known to cause global warming and climate change. The intended meaning likely is that the climatic conditions will worsen in the coming years. Therefore, "worsen" is contextually more appropriate than "improve".

questions.question: Which of the words can fit the blank (A) in the passage?
questions.explanation:
The sentence states that asymmetric federalism has been a positive aspect of India's polity. The missing word should describe something positive about the political structure.

questions.question:
What can be the correct sentence after rearrangement that can fit the blank B?

I. shelter from the powerful storm that slammed (A)/ into the coast of Myanmar. (B)/monasteries, pagodas and schools, seeking(C)/Thousands of people hunkered down in.(D)
II. The wrangling between the Union government (A) / and the Government of the National Capital Territory of Delhi has been (B)/ to lay down the terms of their relationship in the way the territory is governed. (C)/an endless saga for years, and the Supreme Court has repeatedly sought (D)

questions.question: Which of the following statements can fit in the blank C in the given passage?
options: The constitution ensures that there should be legal constraints on the powers of government authorities, especially with respect to the rights of the people.
The Central Government has issued an ordinance recently.
In the latest verdict, a Constitution Bench has ruled that the elected government does indeed have control over administrative services.
The pollution level of Delhi is on the rise.
questions.explanation:
The entire passage revolves around the relationship between the centre and state governments. The passage also talks about the Supreme Court ruling on services.

Option C pertains to the same topic and speaks of a verdict and a constitutional bench that is related to the Supreme Court.

Therefore, C option is the most appropriate answer to the given question.

Meanings of the other options:

  • Option A speaks of the Indian constitution and what it ensures. This is not related to the context.
  • Option B refers to an ordinance by the Central Government. Although we can place it in the blank, the meaning of the sentence as per the context is not clear.
  • Option D contains a statement that speaks of Delhi's pollution level, which is clearly irrelevant to the topic.

Therefore, Option C is the correct answer here.

questions.question: Which of the following words in Sentence D need to be interchanged to make the sentence meaningfully correct?
questions.explanation:
Sentence D:

(D) The Court's (1)attempt verdict rejects the (2) unanimous in reading the phrase as one that (3) imposes an additional (4)limitation on its legislative and executive powers.

Identifying the Issue:

  • "unanimous in reading" does not make sense; instead, it should be "attempt in reading."

Interchanging:

questions.question: Which of the following words in Sentence E need to be interchanged to make the sentence meaningfully correct?
questions.explanation:
Sentence E:
(E) The five-judge Bench ruling again (1) unelected the principle that a (2) representative regime should not be (3) undermined by an (4) underlines administrator.

Identifying the Issue:

Correct Answer: B) 1-4

questions.question: According to the study by BAERI and NASA, which climate impact indicator combines temperature and humidity to assess its effect on the human body?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is (B) Extreme Heat Stress Days. The passage mentions that the researchers paid special attention to two climate impact indicators: the first is heat stress, or the combined effects of temperature and humidity on the human body. The study found that most regions of the world will experience higher heat stress in the 2040s compared to the 1950–1979 baseline.

Option (A) is incorrect because the Fire Weather Index (FWI) is a measurement of extreme fire weather, not the combined effects of temperature and humidity on the human body.

Option (C) is incorrect because the passage does not mention precipitation variation as a climate impact indicator that combines temperature and humidity.

Option (D) is incorrect because solar radiation intensity is not mentioned as a climate impact indicator in this context.

Option (E) is incorrect because wind speed increase is not mentioned as a climate impact indicator that combines temperature and humidity.

questions.question: The study's analysis focused on the impact of extreme events resulting from:
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is (C) Temperature and humidity interactions.

The passage states that the study's analysis focused on the geographic patterns of projected changes to key climate variables, including changes to air temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, solar radiation, and wind speed. It further mentions the researchers paid special attention to heat stress, which is the combined effects of temperature and humidity on the human body.

Options (A), (B), (D), and (E) are incorrect because they are not mentioned as the main focus of the study's analysis in the passage.

questions.question: In accordance with the study's findings, which specific geographic area is anticipated to undergo a considerable escalation in extreme fire weather, as indicated by the augmentation of the Fire Weather Index (FWI)?
questions.explanation:
The passage explicitly supports none of the options, since none name “Amazon,” “Central and Western North America,” or “Mediterranean.”

The passage only mentions the Amazon, Central and Western North America, and the Mediterranean as regions with significant FWI increase. The regions given in the options are not mentioned.

Hence, Option E is the correct answer.

questions.question: Which dataset did the researchers use in their study to examine projected changes in climate variables at a local scale?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is (B) NEX-GDDP.

The passage mentions that the study uses a publicly available NASA dataset, the NASA Earth eXchange – Global Daily Downscaled Projections (NEX-GDDP), which allows for examining projected changes on a local scale.

Options (A), (C), (D), and (E) are incorrect because they are not the dataset mentioned in the passage for this study.

questions.question: What is the main reason for studying climate variables in combination, rather than in isolation, according to Taejin Park from BAERI?
options: To understand the real impact on human lives
To predict the exact timing of extreme events
To reduce the complexity of climate models
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is (C) To understand the real impact on human lives.

The passage quotes Taejin Park as saying, "We wanted to study how these individual climate variables are projected to change and what their combined impacts could mean for people around the world. The changes in one variable can compound the effects of another. We need to look at them together to understand the real impact on human lives."

Options (A), (B), (D), and (E) are incorrect because they either misrepresent Taejin Park's statement or provide reasons that are not in alignment with his explanation in the passage.

questions.question:
Which of the following words can be used to fill the blank (A) as well in the sentences given below?

I.The detective conducted a ________ investigation, leaving no stone unturned in his search for clues.
II.The teacher provided a ________ explanation of the complex scientific concept, ensuring that every student understood it.
questions.explanation:
Out of the given options, only 'Thorough' correctly fills the blank given in the passage as well as the sentences that are given in the question statement.

Both blanks require a word meaning detailed or comprehensive, which is the meaning of 'thorough'

Other words are an incorrect fit:
Smear: coat or mark (something) messily or carelessly with a greasy or sticky substance.
Lucrative: producing a great deal of profit.

Hence, option C is the correct choice.

questions.question: The sentence given in (B) in italics may or may not contain an error. Mark the erroneous part in case there is an error.
options: the first is heat stress or the combine effect of
temperature and humidity on the human body.
questions.explanation:
The error in part (C) is the word "combine," which should be "combined."

The word "combined" is the correct past participle form of the verb "combine," and it should be used here to correctly describe the effect of temperature and humidity on the human body.

Therefore, the corrected sentence reads:

"The researchers paid special attention to two climate impact indicators: the first is heat stress or the combined effect of temperature and humidity on the human body."

Hence, option C is the correct choice.

questions.question:
Directions: In the following question, two statements and five connectors are given. Only one of the connectors from those given can be used to combine the given two statements into one sentence without changing the meaning. Choose that connector as your answer.

(I) As noted in a NITI Aayog report, at least 23 States and Union Territories have prepared a vision document based on SDGs and almost all of them have initiated steps to localise the SDGs.

(II) It has taken a while to get to India’s first Voluntary Local Review at the city level since the efforts to localise the SDGs began.
questions.explanation:
The first statement presents information about the efforts made by at least 23 States and Union Territories to prepare a vision document based on SDGs and localize the SDGs. The second statement introduces a contrasting idea that, despite these efforts, it has taken a while to achieve India's first Voluntary Local Review at the city level.

The connector "Although" is used to introduce a contrasting idea.

In the given question,  “Although” correctly joins the two clauses to show contrast between progress and delay, while keeping the meaning intact and sentence structure grammatical.

By using this connector, the two statements can be combined as follows:

"Although at least 23 States and Union Territories have prepared a vision document based on SDGs and almost all of them have initiated steps to localize the SDGs, it has taken a while to get to India's first Voluntary Local Review at the city level since the efforts to localize the SDGs began."

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, two statements and four connectors are given. Only one of the connectors from those given can be used to combine the given two statements into one sentence without changing the meaning. Choose that connector as your answer. If none of the given connectors are correct, then mark "None of the above" as your answer.

I. So, Google’s story in India is not merely about advertising. “It dominates search, video, payments, maps, and it is well-positioned here especially when factors

II. Low penetration levels, overall economic growth rate and the growth in advertising work in its favour,” says Jaspreet Bindra, Founder of Tech Whisperer UK, a digital transformation and tech advisory.
questions.explanation:
The connector "such as" introduces examples that illustrate the main point. In this context, "such as" is used to introduce examples (low penetration levels, overall economic growth rate, and the growth in advertising) that exemplify why Google's story is not limited to advertising alone. These examples provide specific areas where Google dominates and explain the favorable conditions, contributing to its overall influence in India.

The ratio between the number of girls and boys participating in cricket is 1:2 respectively. Number of girls participating in football is what percent of the number of boys participating in volleyball?

Given total students = 1800

One boy can completea piece of work in  = 300 ×3 =900 days.

One day 1 hour per day work of a boy = 900900=1 unit.

Required days =900300= 3 days.
